text:
alex: heads up — after the calibration rollout at ~1805100000 we're seeing a 12-18% tail-latency regression on INT4 code paths. KV miss rate jumped ~3x in the samples from canary. flame graph points to cutlass::int4_gemm hot path and large stalls in kernel launch retry.

alex: quick perf snippet from the canary profiler:
```
Profile summary (p50/p95/p99): 14ms / 78ms / 220ms (prev: 12/66/186)
KV hit-rate: 0.81 -> 0.62
int4_gemm time contribution: +22%
Kernel chosen: cutlass_int4_sm80 (fallback path on some hosts)
```

maria: which build flags / prober version are on the canary images? could this be arch-detection related?

alex: build info: `git rev-parse --short HEAD` -> `f3b7a2c`
CMake flags: `-DUSE_CUTLASS_INT4=ON -DTRITON_KERNEL_TOGGLE=1 -DARCH_PROBER=v0.3.1 -DCACHE_PREFETCH_WINDOW=8`
I also noticed the arch prober reported sm_80 on a subset of H100 hosts (should be sm_90). looks like the prober logic fell back to sm_80 when the microcode string parsing hit an unexpected token. that caused the runtime to pick cutlass kernels compiled for sm_80 which are suboptimal on sm_90, and the int4 path ends up slower.

kai: hmm. if prober misclassified H100 as sm_80, cutlass config may select different tile sizes and epilogue codegen. can we repro locally by forcing arch env? try `export RW_ARCH=sm_90` + run microbench. also toggle `TRITON_KERNEL_PREFERENCE=triton` to force the Triton kernels and see throughput/latency tradeoffs.

alex: forced Triton on one host — p95 dropped ~10% vs cutlass on that host, but generation quality (rounding noise) for one model variant regressed slightly; not ideal to globally force it. also tried bumping `CACHE_PREFETCH_WINDOW` from 8 -> 32 which reduced KV misses and recouped about 4% on tail.

maria: batching heuristics? if KV misses increase with larger batches, smaller batches might avoid cache churn. what's current max_batch and batch timeout?

alex: current heuristics: max_batch=64, batch_timeout_ms=6, adaptive_batching enabled. when I lower max_batch->32 and batch_timeout_ms->4 in canary the p95 improves but throughput drops ~6% under heavy load. tradeoff between SLO and cost.

perf-bot: automated note: microbench/int4_gemm_sm80 vs sm90 scheduled for 1805124000 (will run on A100/H100 pools).

kai: long-term fix: two-pronged: 1) fix arch prober string parsing + add unit tests for new microcode patterns, 2) update kernel selection to prefer arch-agnostic heuristics when KV-miss-driven tail is detected (i.e., prefer Triton tile that tolerates cache misses). also add an opt-in `PREFETCH_KV_ON_MISS` heuristic to trigger prefetch for cold KV keys.

alex: agreed. quick patch I tested locally:
```
// runtime flag prototype
--kv-prefetch-window=32
--kernel-selection-fallback=triton_when_kv_miss
```
with that the p95 improved ~9% on the canary without global Triton.

maria: can we also add a perf regression test to CI that runs int4_gemm on both sm_80 and sm_90 with calibration snapshots? want to catch calibration -> quantization combos that flip kernel routes.

kai: yes — add a nightly perf job that runs calibration variations (scale-shift extremes) and asserts p95 within 10% of baseline. also add an arch prober fuzz test.

deploy-bot: canary rollback scheduled? @maria @alex please confirm if you want immediate rollback to previous calibration.

alex: hold for 30m while we push prober fix + kernel fallback toggle to canary. if metrics still bad, rollback.

maria: filing follow-ups: #1 prober parsing fix + unit tests, #2 runtime flag `--kv-prefetch-window`, #3 kernel-selection metrics & CI perf test, #4 revert plan if rollback needed. tagging @kai for test harness changes. :memo:

kai: I'll add the nightly perf job and the microbench variants. splitting into small PRs.

alex: thanks — will patch prober and push the runtime toggle to canary (1805123800). monitoring dashboards updated. :thumbsup:

maria: ack.
